value: Low income according to federal poverty guidelines (no percentage stated). The application asks about legal-aid representation and public benefits (SNAP, SSI, TANF, OHP). The court may waive, defer (payment plan, possibly with collection costs), postpone ruling, or deny. A deferral or denial becomes a judgment for the fees. The clerk may decide first, and a denial can be reviewed by a judge (ORS 21.682: party 'unable to pay').

value: Individuals (in person, through a lawyer, or through a non-lawyer representative with personal knowledge of the case and written authorization). Partnerships may appear through a partner, a lawyer, or an employee or agent with personal knowledge and written authorization. Corporations and other entities may appear through an officer, a lawyer, or an employee or agent with personal knowledge and written authorization from an officer. Authorization must be filed before the representative acts and is case by case (no blanket authorizations, no businesses set up to represent others). Minors and incapacitated persons appear through a guardian (Ch. 800). Philadelphia uses an Appointment of Authorized Representative form.

value: MDJ: personal service by the sheriff or a certified constable (the MDJ delivers the complaint to them; a certified constable may serve anywhere in the state; outside the county, through that county's sheriff/constable or, in Philadelphia, the Municipal Court's writ server or sheriff). Or, where the rules allow and at the plaintiff's option, the court mails it by certified mail or a comparable method with a return receipt. Service must be at least 10 days before the hearing. Philadelphia Municipal Court: court service ($27 per Philadelphia address) or out-of-county sheriff ($45).

value: Judge's discretion: no fixed income test on the uniform form. The plaintiff swears that because of poverty they cannot bear the expenses of the case, and lists dependents, employer, net income, benefits (AFDC, SSI, retirement, disability, unemployment, workers' comp), expenses, assets and debts. The judge either allows filing on a pauper's oath or enters a determination of nonindigency with reasons. The plaintiff has a right to a hearing if denied.

value: The clerk issues the civil warrant to whoever the plaintiff designates as authorized to serve process (sheriff, or a private process server, who must give name and address on the return). Or by registered or certified return-receipt mail sent by the plaintiff, attorney, or authorized person; a default judgment on mail service needs a return receipt showing acceptance by the defendant or an authorized person. Process must be served within 60 days of issuance. Sheriff service is typically $52 per defendant (county fee sheets); out-of-county service needs a check to that county's sheriff; service through the Secretary of State ($20) or Commissioner of Insurance ($15) in some cases.
